doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Avoiding drugs, and how drink and dope affected Parker and Tatum
summary: He avoided needles and heavy drink, and says Parker and Tatum played worse when impaired.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, and the remarkable thing is in looking at all of these experiences that were having, you were still so young. You had done so much and you had been with so many bands, but you were so young.
Yeah, well I was anxious to make it [laughter].

Yeah, I really, one thing I can say, I can brag about, that I studied. I didn’t waste too much time like a lot of young guys do. I was fortunate not enough, fortunate to dislike booze that much, and dope, I never liked. Well, I tried dope, I tried, well dope; marijuana, that’s about it. The idea of sticking a needle in your arm, that scared the hell out of me, I wouldn’t do that, I wouldn’t do that…

Right. DeFranco:…and I watched too many guys kill themselves with that. But I did not lack the feeling that booze, excess drinking or dope, gave you; being detached from the world. I didn’t want to be away from the world…
Did it make you feel out of control?
Especially while playing, I wanted to be, I wanted to have the contact with the world while I’m playing. So that was pretty lucky, you know, that that turned out.
Some guys can take dope and play well, you know…
Right, interesting how it affected people…
Different people… Murphy:…effects people so differently…
Yeah. Murphy:…I mean, Charlie Parker and Art Tatum.

Although, Charlie Parker never really did play well when he was stoned, not really. I spent enough time with him to know that. And there again, Art Tatum didn’t play that well when he was drunk, he didn’t take dope too much. But he drank a lot of gin and beer, drank more beer than any one person I can imagine.
You haven’t met enough Irish men. [laughter]
Art Tatum. Murphy:…give him a run for the money.
Boy, I remember doing a session with Art Tatum for Norman Granz and Norman had cases of beer for Art. But he never showed that he was drinking at all, he was always a fantastic player.
